title: Boring neck & calves work + Devon Larratt
summary: NH films his neck and calves isolation work while listening to arm wrestler Devon Larratt discuss the King's Move; the audio is entirely Devon's talk, not NH speaking. Devon explains the history and naming of the King's Move, its risk (willingness to break your arm), safety rules, and argues it is a strong but flawed technique.

claims.claim: NH does isolation work for neck and calves, which he considers boring, while listening to arm wrestling content.
Devon Larratt (whose talk NH plays) says he never defines a 'pure' way to win; he does his best within the rules, whether hook, press, strap or King's Move.

Per Devon Larratt, the King's Move signals willingness to risk breaking your arm, which a mature professional athlete has the right to choose; frame and skeletal strength are a huge part of arm wrestling.
Per Devon Larratt, the King's Move is not an ace but more like a jack (a queen in a strap match), with flaws such as no climbing and lack of shoulder commitment.
